name: watch.window
description: Subscribe to window appear / disappear events. Filter by `title_prefix`, `pid`, or both (both must match); at least one is required, and passing neither returns `invalid_args`. Emits EVENT frames as matching top-level windows are created or destroyed.

title_prefix.description: Prefix filter (case-insensitive). EVENT frames fire only for windows whose title starts with this prefix.

pid.description: Owning-process filter. EVENT frames fire only for windows owned by this process id. Browsers that hand off to an already-running instance (launching `msedge.exe` while Edge is open) open the window in a different process, so this filter never fires for them.

x-event-schema.description: EVENT frames emitted on window create / destroy.

kind.description: `created` when a window appears; `destroyed` when it disappears.

title.description: Window title at the moment of the event. Empty string for windows without a title.

x-implementations.name: set_winevent_hook
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SetWinEventHook(EVENT_OBJECT_CREATE | EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROY, WINEVENT_OUTOFCONTEXT)`. NT 5+ — out-of-process hook with no DLL injection. Filtered to top-level windows, title_prefix and pid in the agent's hook callback; pid via GetWindowThreadProcessId.

x-implementations.name: enum_windows_poll
x-implementations.description: Polling fallback for NT 4 / 9x where SetWinEventHook is unavailable. EnumWindows every 250 ms; diff against previous snapshot to compute appear/disappear.

windows-modern.description: SetWinEventHook with EVENT_OBJECT_CREATE / EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROY. Out-of-process, no DLL injection. Title prefix and pid filtered in the agent's callback before emitting EVENTs.

windows-classic.description: SetWinEventHook on NT 5+; polling EnumWindows on NT 4 / 9x. The polling fallback may miss short-lived windows that appear and disappear within a single 250 ms interval.
